summary: In a warm Sunday morning scene on a veranda, Lexy and Captain Grey sit after breakfast with Dr. Quelton, whose manner is reassuring. Lexy presses Captain Grey about being kept from seeing his sister, whom no one is allowed to visit, and urges him to assert himself. Captain Grey hesitates, citing propriety and the awkwardness of challenging his brother-in-law's house, but they go upstairs to try to see her, where a nurse answers the door.
one_line: On a quiet Sunday at Dr. Quelton's house, Lexy urges Captain Grey to defy the rules and visit his sister, who is kept from visitors.
key_facts: Lexy and Captain Grey sat together on the veranda in the warm morning sunshine after breakfast in the dining room.
Dr. Quelton was courteous, affable and very attentive to his guests at breakfast.
Church bells were ringing in the far distance on a Sunday tranquillity over the country.
Lexy believed her time in the house would not be long because she had caused Dr. Quelton an anxiety he could not conceal.
Lexy said Captain Grey was not allowed to see his sister and that no one could see her.
Captain Grey was not allowed to call in another doctor.
Captain Grey said that in her husband's house he could not make a row.
Lexy asked, 'Why can't you?' and the question left Captain Grey startled and uneasy.
Lexy suggested he put on his best commanding officer's air and said there was nothing she would stop at.
Lexy advised Captain Grey to 'Laugh it off' if Dr. Quelton objected.
Captain Grey said, 'Suppose he hoofs us out of the house?'
Lexy said, 'Let's try it, anyhow,' and Captain Grey agreed with 'Right-o!'
They went upstairs and down the hall of the other wing, opposite Lexy's room.
A quiet, middle-aged little nurse came out when Captain Grey knocked on a door.
Captain Grey said he would pop in to see how his sister was getting on.
